results.reader_title: European research organisations object to EIC intellectual property rules
results.reader_what: Signatory associations argue EIC Pathfinder and Transition IP provisions conflict with institutional and national rules and deter participation.
results.reader_why: IP terms shape whether European research organisations take part in EIC funding at all.
results.reader_more: Associations of research-performing organisations and knowledge transfer professionals jointly urged the European Commission to apply the standard Horizon Europe intellectual property rules to European Innovation Council Transition and Pathfinder projects, rather than the special provisions then in force. Those provisions grant EIC inventors indefinite, royalty-free access rights for exploitation, with royalties shared only where the employing organisation supports the inventor's exploitation. The signatories argue these terms conflict with institutional, national and regional rules, hindering their members' participation in the EIC, and may undermine their own efforts to maximise exploitation of research results. They tie the argument to the Commission's own knowledge valorisation guiding principles, Council conclusions on the New European Innovation Agenda and a European Parliament report on EIC implementation.
